findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, oversized file)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and propagate with ? or explicit map_err

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value or out-of-range value
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line aborts the entire load instead of reporting which record is invalid
findings.fix: use try_fold over lines, parse with map_err returning a typed ParseError, and include line/field context

findings.problem: as u16 is an unchecked lossy cast from u32 that silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value in the CSV silently wraps to an incorrect u16, corrupting data without any error signal
findings.fix: use u32::try_into().map_err(...) or u16::try_from() to return a typed error on overflow

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a hidden side effect inside a pure-looking data parser
findings.failure_mode: I/O is embedded in the core parsing logic, making the function non-deterministic, untestable in isolation, and producing stdout pollution when used as a library
findings.fix: remove println!; if telemetry is needed, return a separate metadata vector or pass an explicit sink callback in the shell layer

findings.problem: parts[0] is unchecked indexing into a Vec that may have fewer than 1 element
findings.failure_mode: a blank line or single-field CSV line panics on index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and pattern-match the two-field result, or guard with parts.get(0).ok_or(...)

findings.problem: parts[1] is unchecked indexing into a Vec that may have fewer than 2 elements
findings.failure_mode: a line missing the second CSV field panics on index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and destructure the two-field result explicitly

findings.problem: Collecting all parts into Vec<String> with .collect() allocates heap memory for every line
findings.failure_mode: high line counts cause excessive heap allocations and GC pressure; each line creates multiple String allocations for trimmed copies
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to get two &str fragments, trim them in place, and avoid Vec/String collection entirely

findings.problem: Function returns Vec<Record> with no try_reserve or capacity hint
findings.failure_mode: frequent reallocations as the vector grows, especially bad for large sensor files
findings.fix: accept a line count hint or use try_reserve before collecting; or return Result with capacity estimation

findings.problem: I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, logging, and type conversion are all mixed into a single function
findings.failure_mode: violates functional core / imperative shell; the pure parsing logic cannot be unit-tested without a real file on disk; side effects are inseparable from computation
findings.fix: split into (a) shell: fn load_sensors(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> that reads and delegates, and (b) core: fn parse_records(lines: impl IntoIterator<Item=&str>) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> that is pure and testable
